items.t: Investor AB stock gains 1.57% during dividend week
sum: Investor AB stock gained 1.57 percent over the week from Monday, November 9, through Friday, November 13, as the holding company's second-dividend timetable moved through two key dates. Investor's financial calendar lists November 9 as the record day and says the second dividend was expected to be paid by Euroclear Sweden AB on November 12.

Investor AB stock traded at 39.74 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:06 CET on Saturday, November 14, 0.86 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, November 13. The prior Xetra close was 38.79 euros on Friday, November 6, while the share closed at 39.40 euros on Friday, November 13, according to Yahoo Finance.

Investor's latest corporate messaging continues to center on active ownership, portfolio development and sustainable growth across its listed and privately held companies. The company also highlights its ability to generate cash flow, support portfolio companies and maintain dividend capacity.

The scheduled calendar points to the next major reporting date on January 22, 2027, when Investor is due to publish its Year-End Report 2026. Until then, investors are likely to focus on portfolio developments, capital allocation and the relationship between the share price and the company's net asset value.
Investor AB trades within the wider Swedish equity market context covered by Current market reports.

items.t: Investor AB stock shifts toward portfolio execution after update
sum: Investor hosted its Capital Markets Update on November 4, 2026, focusing on strategy, capital allocation and its three business areas. The company said the event was intended to provide an update on its priorities and portfolio development, according to Investor AB's Capital Markets Days page.

On Friday, November 13, 2026, at 12:10 CET, Investor AB B traded at 39.38 euros on Lang & Schwarz. The quote reflects the B share identified by ISIN SE0015811963; no directional comparison is made here with an Xetra close.

Investor's latest Interim Management Statement for January-September 2026 put adjusted net asset value at SEK 1,258.0 billion on September 30, equal to SEK 411 per share. Adjusted NAV increased 4 percent during the third quarter, according to the company's investor materials.

The holding company said its portfolio companies are balancing current operating performance with investment in innovation, particularly in artificial intelligence. Investor's management also linked long-term success to faster innovation, more effective investment and the ability to scale new technologies profitably.

The November 4 update shifts the focus from communicating the strategy to executing it across the portfolio. For investors, the key issue is how effectively Investor converts recurring cash flow, ownership influence and portfolio company performance into further NAV growth and dividends.

Investor is organized around Listed Companies, Patricia Industries and Investments in EQT. The structure gives the group exposure to listed holdings and wholly or partly owned businesses, while its engaged-ownership model leaves portfolio performance and capital allocation as the main drivers of future results.
Investor AB is listed in Sweden, and broader market developments can be followed through the OMXS30 market overview.

GBL stock clears Recordati threshold with CVC for delisting path
sum: Groupe Bruxelles Lambert and private-equity firm CVC secured more than 90 percent of Recordati at the end of the takeover offer period, Reuters reported on November 9, 2026. The result clears the regulatory threshold for a squeeze-out of remaining minority shareholders and creates a path toward delisting the Italian pharmaceutical company from Euronext Milan.

The crossing of the threshold gives the offeror access to the compulsory purchase mechanisms under Italian takeover law. Recordati shareholders who did not tender their shares may therefore face a subsequent buyout process, while the remaining listed shares could be removed from trading after the required steps are completed.

The transaction matters for GBL because Recordati is part of its investment portfolio. Moving the holding from a listed position into a privately controlled company could change how the asset is reflected in GBL's future net asset value. The effect will depend on the final transaction terms and the valuation applied after completion.

GBL is a Brussels-based investment holding company with investments across listed and private businesses. Its portfolio includes interests in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, consumer goods and industrial activities, giving the group broader exposure than a single-industry company.

In the European investment-company segment, GBL competes for shareholder capital with diversified groups such as Eurazeo, Wendel and Investor AB. GBL is distinguished by its Belgian base and its mix of listed holdings and direct private investments.
European equity markets remain the broader backdrop for diversified investment companies. Current Euro Stoxx 50 market reports provide the relevant regional context.

Here are 5 of the most popular shares bought in a Stocks and Shares ISA this year
sum: The Stocks and Shares ISA is one of the best tools UK investors have for building wealth almost completely tax-free, as every penny of capital gains and dividends stays in your pocket.

However, even with a powerful tool like an ISA, that still begs the question which stocks an investor should buy? After all, there are thousands of companies to choose from across stock exchanges around the world. And it can be quite daunting to try and figure out where the best place is to start.

This is where looking at what other investors are buying can be a helpful starting point. And thanks to data from Interactive Investor, we know that five of the most popular shares being bought by UK investors this year are:

Please note that tax treatment depends on the individual circumstances of each client and may be subject to change in future. The content in this article is provided for information purposes only. It is not intended to be, neither does it constitute, any form of tax advice. Readers are responsible for carrying out their own due diligence and for obtaining professional advice before making any investment decisions.

GCM Resources, Rolls-Royce and Nvidia are punchy growth stories, riding the tailwinds of booming aerospace and artificial intelligence (AI) markets. Legal & General and Glencore offer something different: higher-yielding income that pays investors for their patience.

This suggests that ISA investors are pairing potentially explosive growth opportunities with chunky passive income opportunities. And by concentrating capital into large-cap companies, investors are seemingly trying to keep risk in check. The sole outlier is GCM Resources, which is a penny stock and a different beast entirely.

As a quick introduction, GCM owns the Phulbari Coal and Power Project in north-west Bangladesh. The site holds an estimated 572 million tonnes of coal just waiting to be extracted. And just to put that number into perspective, management has estimated that it's sufficient to meet just over 60% of Bangladesh's domestic coal power demand.

Investor AB stock enters strategy execution phase after update
sum: Investor AB held its Capital Markets Update on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, putting strategy, capital allocation and the development of its portfolio companies at the center of the investor discussion. The company made the presentation materials available through its Capital Markets Update 2026 page.

Investor describes its long-term investment case through superior returns, sustainable growth, proprietary cash flow and efficient operations. The Swedish holding company links future growth at its portfolio companies to structural trends including demographics, automation, digitalization and the green transition.

The format of the update also underscores Investor's engaged-ownership model. Presentations covered listed companies, investments in EQT, Patricia Industries and several portfolio companies, including Sarnova, BraunAbility, Laborie, Nova Biomedical and Mölnlycke. That breadth keeps execution at individual holdings central to the investment debate.

On its investors and media page, Investor reported adjusted net asset value of 1,258.0 billion SEK and NAV per share of 411 SEK for the January-September 2026 period. NAV is a central reference for investors because the holding company's market quotation reflects the portfolio's underlying assets as well as expectations for future value creation.

CEO Christian Cederholm said the companies were balancing current performance with investment in innovation, particularly around artificial intelligence, to secure profitable long-term growth. For shareholders, the next test is whether those investments translate into stronger earnings and sustained NAV growth rather than only higher spending.
The real-time quote of Investor AB stock traded at 38.94 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:49 CET on Monday, November 9, 2026.

My Stocks and Shares ISA has tanked! Here’s what I’m doing
sum: It has been a very difficult spell for my Stocks and Shares ISA recently. Many of my largest holdings have tanked as growth and AI/tech stocks have sold off aggressively. Thursday (5 November) was particularly brutal.
Adding salt to the wounds, even 'boring' FTSE 100 stalwarts such as HSBC and BAE Systems have been struggling. Both of these are roughly 20% below their summer highs.
The first thing I need to remember is that volatility and periods of poor performance are par for the course for a long-term investor.
My holding period for a stock is three-to-five years (ideally longer). Therefore, what happens over three-to-five months isn't that important in the grand scheme of things.
That said, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't bothered when my portfolio rapidly declines in value. I don't like it. But I know it's the price of admission to the stock market.

As always, there's a Warren Buffett quote that clarifies things: "You've got to be prepared, when you buy a stock, to have it go down 50% — or more — and be comfortable with it, as long as you're comfortable with the holding."
Another thing I like to do at times like this is to put things into perspective. Returning to HSBC and BAE, for example, these UK shares had a fantastic 2025. So did Rolls-Royce.

Albertsons (ACI) Stock Still Looks Undervalued On Its 44% Five Year Fall
sum: Albertsons Companies shares have fallen a long way over the past few years, yet the supermarket operator still generates substantial revenue from its grocery and pharmacy network. That mix of a weaker share price and meaningful sales base puts a simple question in front of you as an investor: whether today's valuation really lines up with the business it is doing at the checkout.
- The stock is down 44.0% over the past 5 years, which puts extra focus on whether the current market value is still in step with the sales the chain is producing.

- Recent headlines include a US$900m opioid-related judgment and a reshaped board that now features an executive chair. These developments can influence future cash needs, legal expenses, and how much of Albertsons' sales ultimately turn into value for shareholders.
- Your read on Albertsons Companies is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Albertsons Companies's shares could be worth.
The issue now is whether the current Albertsons share price is appropriately supported by its sales when you line it up against the Fair Ratio benchmark.
To see how Albertsons Companies compares with other businesses where sales and valuation are under the microscope, review it alongside 39 high quality undervalued stocks.

The P/S ratio fits Albertsons Companies because grocery chains are often judged on how much value the market assigns to each dollar of sales. On that yardstick, the current P/S of 0.1x is far below the Consumer Retailing industry average of 0.4x and well under the broader peer group near 1.4x. That gap suggests investors are assigning a relatively low price tag to Albertsons' revenue stream compared with many other listed retailers.

INQ Group AB (publ) raises SEK 7 million under convertible loan facility from new US-based investment manager
sum: INQ Group AB (publ) ("INQ" or the "Company"), listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ticker: INQ), announces that it has raised SEK 7,000,000 of additional capital under its existing secured convertible loan facility from a US-based investment manager.
The new financing is being completed on the same principal terms as the Company's most recently announced tranche of the facility, including a conversion price of SEK 0.16 per share.

The additional capital follows the conversion of substantially all of the Company's earlier convertible debt under Tranches 1 through 5. Following those conversions, approximately USD 1.55 million of convertible principal remained outstanding. The SEK 7,000,000 financing announced today will be added to that outstanding balance.
The financing further strengthens INQ's working capital position as the Company continues the commercialisation and expansion of its consumer, enterprise and education businesses.

Under the terms of the new tranche, the investor is entitled to convert outstanding principal together with accrued and unpaid interest into newly issued ordinary shares in INQ at a conversion price of SEK 0.16 per share, subject to customary adjustments.

The new tranche will also be mandatorily converted at the same conversion price upon completion of a qualified equity financing of at least USD 3 million equivalent at a subscription price of at least SEK 0.22 per share.

In connection with the new tranche, the investor will receive warrants for no further consideration with a value equal to 20 per cent of the amount funded. The warrants will entitle the holder to subscribe for new ordinary shares in INQ at a subscription price of SEK 0.32 per share for a period of two years. The final number of warrants and underlying shares will be determined in accordance with the terms of the financing.

items.t: Tesco (LSE:TSCO) Stock May Be 25% Undervalued Despite €1.7b Asset Sale
sum: Tesco has delivered strong share price returns in recent years, which puts a sharper focus on whether the cash the business generates can support where the stock now trades. With investors also weighing fresh corporate moves, the question is how much of the supermarket group's future cash flows are effectively being priced in today.
- Over the past 5 years the stock has returned 140.9%, so a lot of investor capital now hinges on how reliably Tesco can turn its operations into cash over the coming years.

- The agreed €1.7b sale of its Czech and Slovak businesses, with most of the roughly €1.2b net proceeds earmarked for share buybacks, can reshape Tesco's future cash flow profile by concentrating on UK and Irish operations while reducing the share count.
- Prefer to judge Tesco on earnings? See what Tesco's 17.9x P/E says about the price.

If you are weighing Tesco against other options that also screen on valuation and fundamentals, it can help to compare it with companies in the 13 high quality undervalued stocks.

sum: Investor AB's next major investor event is the Capital Markets Update scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, 2026, according to Vontobel Markets. The meeting gives investors a near-term opportunity to assess the holding company's portfolio priorities after its third-quarter update.

Investor's adjusted net asset value reached SEK 411 per share on September 30, 2026, up 4 percent during the third quarter and 17 percent since the start of the year. The figure exceeded the 11 percent total return delivered by the SIXRX index over the same nine-month period.

Patricia Industries was the strongest part of the portfolio in the quarter. Its private holdings generated a 15 percent total return, while adjusted EBITA increased 26 percent year over year. Aggregate sales at the private subsidiaries grew 12 percent, including 7 percent organic growth in constant currencies.

The November 4 update is expected to provide further strategic detail on Mölnlycke's planned separation into two businesses and on Patricia Industries' acquisition pipeline. The event may also help investors assess whether the recent recovery in Investor's EQT investments can continue after a difficult nine-month period.

items.t: First Solar slides 10% as Jefferies downgrades stock on lower booking visiblity
sum: Investing.com -- Shares of First Solar slumped 10% on Wed. after analysts at Jefferies said expectations for policy-driven upside in 2026 look richer than the likely reality as booking visibility weakens, and downgraded stock to Hold.
Optimism around Section 232 tariffs is likely to underwhelm investors, according to Jefferies.

The risk of carve-outs for Germany and other trading partners could dilute pricing benefits, alongside developers moving procurement decisions ahead of potential duties and foreign entity of concern rules.
These dynamics limit how much pricing uplift First Solar can realistically capture, raising downside risk to 2026 volume assumptions.
Jefferies said visibility into 2026 bookings remains limited after a difficult 2025 that saw guidance cuts, de-bookings and margin pressure.

Shares have rallied to 52-week highs, with gains of around 37% in last six months, as some regulatory headwinds eased. Jefferies sees little incremental policy support left to justify current valuations.
Investor focus is likely to shift toward execution and use of cash rather than further regulatory upside.
